eligibility.quote: problem confirmed, changing system time causes this issue. (cyclonedds has the same problem)

failed_conditions.quote:
When you call `rcl_wait()`, the timeout passed to `rmw_wait()` is calculated [like](https://github.com/ros2/rcl/blob/c83119c826c75fbaf6e741658927a953318832ad/rcl/src/rcl/wait.c#L546-L582):

`min(rcl_wait_timeout, minimal_timeout_to_next_timer_trigger)`

but the timer might be using a different clock that the one `rmw_wait()` uses ....

loudness.quote: Timer callback execution waits 5 seconds when the system timer is adjusted to backward.

resolution.quote:
I have confirmed that the bug is fixed in the following environments.

- Ubuntu22.04
- rolling
- rmw_fastrtps_cpp
- (docker ros2:nightly [DIGEST:9c3250e5675f])

notes: Verified via gh api: issue body (reproducer with `sudo date -s` and the 5 s stall), fujitatomoya's confirmation, ivanpauno's full timeout-calculation comment, Barry-Xu-2018's gcc-10 FUTEX_CLOCK_REALTIME finding, jwakely's pthreads analysis, the fix-confirmation comment, and the rmw PR #316 diff changing rmw.h from 'Elapsed time is measured against the system clock.' to 'Elapsed time should be measured using a monotonic clock, though rmw implementations could use a different one.' Class 'other' is right: the condition is the clock base of the timeout duration crossing rcl -> rmw_wait, which no listed class names. Elements verdict disagree: the quoted condition is about the timeout argument of rmw_wait, so the implicated element is api:rmw_wait, not api:rmw_create_wait_set (the wait set is created without any timeout or clock involvement). Resolution 'recommended' is correct: the reporter's confirmation names no git revision of either unit (docker digest only), and rmw_fastrtps itself was never edited.
